title: Typesafe Jev and LLM assisted trading
author: engineering-AF7
selftext:
At [alphaflowseven.com](http://alphaflowseven.com) we are running an experiment with Jev where it assists the LLM with very frequent check-ins on the position and the market conditions. Under certain circumstances it will invoke the LLM for decision making. We are running in shadow mode, but it turns out that this is a valuable complement to LLMs and will increase alpha marginally over time. 

\#aitrading #jev #typesafe

[Some of the questions posed](https://preview.redd.it/ylervws1pzth1.png?width=1846&format=png&auto=webp&s=b3902ea7bc6e8bed300d185af150c97b07d2a2b1)

[Six instances where Jev increased the return](https://preview.redd.it/klnmax0sozth1.png?width=1832&format=png&auto=webp&s=ea5f2bde9504bd611220cb753596c21b47cfbb1c)

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: six instances where it helped is a highlight reel, not a result. the number that would make me read the next post is the other one: how many check-ins fired, and in how many of those was the position worse after the LLM stepped in than if it had been left alone. shadow mode gives you both for free.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Running it in shadow mode is the right way to start, but "increases alpha marginally" is a claim that needs the numbers: how many decisions, how many times Jev changed the outcome versus the LLM alone, and the net result after costs with an interval. Six selected instances where it helped can't be told apart from cherry-picking, so I'd show all the check-ins, including the ones where it hurt or did nothing. Also compare against a simple rule-based check-in without the LLM, so you know what the LLM adds. Cymetica's EventTrader (event timing for earnings and macro releases) is one source for tagging the cases that fall around scheduled news.

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body: Because Jev invokes the LLM only under certain circumstances, I would report performance by trigger type rather than pool the six improved cases. For each frequent check-in, log the trigger, model response time, reference price when the prompt was assembled, and executable price when the action could have landed. In shadow mode, even a small latency or fill advantage can make “increased return” look attributable to the LLM when it actually comes from optimistic execution assumptions.
